extracted.intended_audience: Area Chairs (ACs) for ICML 2026 / ICML program committee members
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and evaluation criteria for Area Chairs handling paper assignments, ensuring review quality, triaging ethics/integrity issues, recruiting emergency reviewers, and writing meta-reviews and recommendations for ICML 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicate areas of expertise and bid on submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate your areas of research expertise, and “bid” on submissions to meta-review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bidding is done within OpenReview on submission abstracts and is used, in part, to help assign submissions to ACs during the bidding period (dates provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Check meta-reviewing assignments and report problems to SAC
rubrics_metrics.description: Check your meta-reviewing assignments and notify your Senior Area Chair (SAC) of any problems (e.g., conflicts of interest).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your SAC is the first point of contact for issues; for position track papers contact position track chairs directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure reviewer assignment quality (qualified reviewers per paper)
rubrics_metrics.description: Check that each assigned submission is assigned four qualified reviewers (we may revise this), and adjust assignments as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not make more than two reviewer substitutions per submission; if additional substitutions are absolutely necessary, obtain approval from your SAC. Change sort order in OpenReview to 'Affinity Score' or another informative sort to find relevant reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure each submission receives at least three high-quality reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that each assigned submission receives at least three high-quality reviews, each written in a respectful and professional manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check reviews as they arrive; ask reviewers to revise reviews to add justification, clarify points or questions, or adjust tone/language. If reviewers are missing by the deadline, contact them to determine whether to recruit emergency reviewers. Try to avoid having too many (e.g., 5+) reviewers for a single submission; if that occurs, tell authors which reviews to prioritize and consider this when forming the meta-review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruit emergency reviewers when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Recruit emergency reviewers as needed to ensure three high-quality reviews are in place before the author response period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First contact potential emergency reviewers by email to check willingness and a meaningful deadline before sending the OpenReview invite. You can invite from the emergency reviewer pool or add a new external reviewer (requires SAC). Do not invite reviewers who have reached their quota; use the 'Show reviewers with fewer than max assigned papers' checkbox to find available reviewers. As a last resort you may add yourself as a reviewer by asking your SAC to invite you as an external reviewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage reviewers in discussions and ensure they read author responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage and facilitate reviewer discussions and ensure reviewers read and acknowledge authors' responses by the stated deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage reviewers to discuss contradictions and unclear points via notes on OpenReview (visible only to Reviewers/ACs). AC-reviewer discussions are not visible to authors. Ensure reviewers update their reviews appropriately after discussions; reviewers are required to provide a final justification accounting for the rebuttal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compose informed meta-reviews and accept/reject recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Carefully read the reviews and discussions to make accept/reject recommendations and compose informed meta-reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meta-reviews should summarize key points that justify your recommendation, drawn from reviews and anonymized discussions. Use review content (not just aggregate scores) to form recommendations. Submit meta-reviews and recommendations by the deadline. If your reasoning is based on your own reading rather than the reviews, append a separate review-like section as evidence and clearly separate it from the meta-review proper. If your meta-review goes against reviewer consensus, ensure your reasoning is extra solid. SAC may request clarifications or calibration after submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review tone and structure best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Write meta-reviews that are firm in argument but empathetic and professional in tone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid phrases like 'the paper does not pass the bar for ICML' or 'only accept if there is enough space'. Provide clear arguments along paper evaluation axes and, for rejections, a suggested template that lists up to three major reasons supported by arguments in the reviews or your reading; if promising, encourage revision and resubmission. If rejection reasoning arose primarily from your reading/discussion rather than reviews, add explicit supporting paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance criteria high-level
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers that are technically sound, well-written, non-redundant with previous research, and useful to at least some fraction of the ICML community should be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these axes when forming acceptance recommendations and explain how the paper meets or fails these criteria in the meta-review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide reviewer ratings/feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide ratings of the reviewers for your assigned submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ratings help highlight reviewers who exceed expectations and identify those who are delinquent or shirk responsibilities. If unsure how to rate, ask your SAC for advice. The expectation is that the majority of reviewers will 'meet expectations'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling suspected LLM-generated reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat reviews at face value; do not disregard reviews solely due to evidence of LLM use (e.g., watermark phrases) under Policy B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers following Policy A are not allowed to use Generative AI. If you see severe evidence of AI-generated reviews (hallucinated citations, AI artifacts beyond common phrases), report it to program chairs and the integrity chair via the Ethics Violation Reporting form. Because the reviewers' assigned LLM policies are not visible to ACs, treat all reviewers uniformly. Report concerns that suggest full delegation of review writing to Generative AI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling hallucinated references
rubrics_metrics.description: If you see at least 2 hallucinated references (or at least 1 hallucinated reference plus additional evidence of AI slop), email the program chairs but continue to review the paper as usual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow ICLR 2026 guidance: a reference is hallucinated if you cannot find any document/publication with a title near the one provided. Minor title differences or small author-name misspellings are not hallucinations. Swapped author lists or incorrect venue for a real publication are not hallucinations (tell authors to fix). Added nonexistent authors or a nonexistent venue are hallucinations. Generic references that do not point to a real document (e.g., 'GPT-4o, OpenAI et al. 2024') are fine. If unsure, err on the side of caution and bring to your SAC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics triage responsibilities (categorization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Triage reviewer-flagged ethical concerns by selecting one of the provided categories for each paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categories: 'No action necessary'; 'The ethical issue requires no further discussion'; 'AC involvement' (remediation handled by reviewers/authors); 'The ethical issue is not being adequately addressed but AC can manage'; 'Ethics review needed' (forward to ethics reviewers); 'Integrity review needed' (plagiarism/AI-generated paper, escalate to Program Chairs). Select the category matching your judgment; for 'ethics review needed' specify relevant area to route to ethics reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics review process and AC role
rubrics_metrics.description: If an ethics review is needed, the paper is forwarded to ethics reviewers who provide feedback and recommended mitigations; ACs coordinate remediation and relay feedback to authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect two ethics reviews returned under tight timelines; ethics reviewers should provide constructive feedback and possible remediations. If ethics reviewers find an unremediable issue, an Ethics Chair will serve as a third reviewer and recommend how to proceed. Final accept/reject decisions are made by Program Chairs with input from ACs and the reviewing ethics chair.

rubrics_metrics.name: AC prohibition on using Generative AI in AC workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of Generative AI tools in the AC workflow is not permitted in any form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICML prohibits ACs from using Generative AI tools. Reviewers may be allowed under Policies A or B with constraints; because reviewer LLM policy assignments are not visible to ACs, treat reviews uniformly. Report suspected unethical use of Generative AI via the Ethics Violation Reporting form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure reviewers provide final justification for their recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are required to provide a final justification describing the reasoning behind their final recommendation and accounting for the rebuttal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACs should work with reviewers to ensure this final justification is entered in a timely manner and appropriately reflects the author-reviewer discussions. This is new this year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow discussion protocol and limit rounds of communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the protocol of the Author-Reviewer discussions is followed; rounds of communication are limited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage timely and focused exchanges. Keep in mind limits on communication rounds and help prioritize important discussion topics; AC-reviewer discussions are private (not visible to authors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Modify reviewer assignments via OpenReview correctly
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Area Chair Console's 'Modify Reviewer Assignments' interface to un-assign, filter, sort, and add reviewers for a paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To un-assign a reviewer, click the 'Trash' icon. Filter by 'Only show reviewers with fewer than max assigned papers' to avoid overloading reviewers. Sort by Affinity or Bids rather than default 'Assignment' to surface relevant reviewers. When adding a reviewer, click 'Assign' / 'Invite Assignment'. Note that OpenReview sends an automatic invitation email; also contact potential reviewers directly first.
